findings.title: Filial care bounded by non-coercive character
findings.claim: بَرًّا بِوَالِدَيْهِ, جَبَّارًا, and عَصِيًّا together portray Yahya's goodness toward his parents as a form of strength that does not become coercive domination or refusal of a binding command; the near-parallel in 19:32 makes this a recurring prophetic-family relation within the supplied wider surface.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers are the parent-directed filial facet of بَرًّا at 19:14:1:2, the will-suppressing coercion facet of جَبَّارًا at 19:14:5:1, and the departure-from-obedience facet of عَصِيًّا at 19:14:6:1. The exact 19:32 wording repeats filial goodness beside the denial of coercive character, 50:45 supplies an independently stated non-jabbār boundary for authority, and 18:69 supplies an explicit obedience contrast; their contact changes the portrait from a list of separate virtues into a relational account of how received power is lived among family.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see parental goodness as more than warmth or courtesy: the sentence presents power as ethically bounded by care for the parents' relation and by freedom from forced submission or deliberate defiance.
findings.containment: 19:32 is used as a bounded same-surah parallel, while its target morphology and lexical analysis are not supplied. 50:45 contributes only the non-coercive authority boundary, and 18:69 only a broad obedience contrast without a filial setting. The finding does not activate the other available branches of these roots, import a divine coercion claim, or state a complete surah thesis.
